name: DNSP-11

lead: DNSP-11 is an 11-amino-acid peptide derived from the precursor region of GDNF, a protein that supports dopamine neurons. People in nootropic circles discuss it for dopamine neuron support and possible brain and mood benefits.

It was proposed as a smaller, easier-to-deliver alternative to full-length GDNF for Parkinson's disease research. In rat experiments it changed dopamine neuron function and increased ERK 1/2 signalling in cells. Published studies are in cells, rats and rhesus macaques, delivered directly to the brain or repeatedly through the nose. No human trials were found and no appearance data exist.

paras: It appears in longevity and nootropic peptide catalogues. No established human routine or timeline exists.
Its safety in humans has not been studied in published trials. It is not an approved drug, and animal findings do not establish human effects.

angle.text: DNSP-11 is an experimental GDNF-derived peptide discussed in nootropic circles for dopamine neuron support, brain and mood. No appearance use is documented; it has been studied in rats and monkeys with no human trials.

lead: DNSP-11 (dopamine neuron stimulating peptide-11) is an experimental 11-amino-acid peptide that researchers derived from the pro-region of glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF). It was proposed as a smaller, easier-to-deliver alternative to full-length GDNF, which has shown protective effects on dopamine neurons in animal models and in some Parkinson's disease trials but is difficult to deliver to the brain because of its size [1][2].

Published work on DNSP-11 consists of cell-culture and animal studies, including rats and rhesus macaques, in which the peptide has been given directly to the brain or repeatedly through the nose [1][3][2][4]. No human clinical trial of DNSP-11 appears in the sources reviewed here. It is not an approved drug, and the sources contain no evidence about any effect on appearance.

The compound is discussed in this wiki because it is a neurotrophic peptide of the kind that appears in longevity and nootropic peptide catalogues. The sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum discussion of it.

paras: Glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) supports the survival of dopamine neurons and was the first member of its protein family to be identified, in 1991. Clinical trials of delivering GDNF to the brains of people with Parkinson's disease have produced mixed results; in one five-year randomized trial in Bristol the GDNF group did not differ statistically from placebo [5]. Delivery is the main obstacle, which motivated work on smaller fragments [1][3].

A model of how the human GDNF precursor is processed proposes that cleavage of the pro-region yields smaller amidated peptides with biological activity, including an 11-amino-acid peptide named DNSP-11 [1][4]. In rat studies, a single dose delivered to the substantia nigra altered dopamine neuron function, and cell experiments showed increased ERK 1/2 phosphorylation [4]. A comparison of three synthetic peptides derived from the pro- and mature GDNF sequence evaluated their physical properties and protective activity in vitro [6].

No studies found in humans. Research is limited to cell and animal work. A 2015 rat study developed a method for repeated intranasal delivery of DNSP-11 in normal rats and a unilateral model of Parkinson's disease [3], and a 2018 study applied a repeated intranasal method to awake rhesus macaques [2]. A 2019 study mapped where an antibody to DNSP-11 labels tissue in the rat brain [7]. These are preclinical studies and do not establish effects in people.
DNSP-11 is not an approved medicine in any jurisdiction mentioned in the sources. No community discussion of it was found in the sources reviewed, and no use for appearance purposes is documented.
